question.prompt: Elmer the emu takes \(44\) equal strides to walk between consecutive telephone poles on a rural road. Oscar the ostrich can cover the same distance in \(12\) equal leaps. The telephone poles are evenly spaced, and the \(41\)st pole along this road is exactly one mile (\(5280\) feet) from the first pole. How much longer, in feet, is Oscar’s leap than Elmer’s stride?

solutions.explanation:
There are \(40\) gaps between the first and forty-first telephone poles. Each gap is
\[
\frac{5280}{40}=132\text{ feet}.
\]
Oscar covers one gap in \(12\) leaps, so each leap is \(132/12=11\) feet long. Elmer covers it in \(44\) strides, so each stride is \(132/44=3\) feet long. Oscar's leap is longer by \(11-3=\boxed{8}\) feet, choice B.
solutions.title: Count gaps and compare equal-distance step counts
